newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Ldn stocks hit peak, others make big gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ldn stocks hit peak, others make big gains.

text.p: London stocks stormed to yet another trading record as the Bank of England signalled that Thursday's interest rate rise would be the last in the currenct cycle.

Other European bourses also chalked up big gains. Frankfurt climbed two percent to within sight of its all-time highs and Paris rose one percent, swept along by Europe's bullish mood and a strong Wall Street opening.

But in currency markets, sterling slumped after the Bank of England raised rates to 7.0 from 6.75 percent, saying they were now at levels consistent with government inflation targets. Traders took this as a signal that rates had peaked and dumped pounds.

It was the fourth rise in as many months but the hints that rates would be held for the time being was good news for British exporters whose profits have been hit by a soaring pound and helped lift the market.
"It's comforting as it's probably meant to be that there won't be any more rises in the short term," said a dealer.
The stock market immediately rebounded from negative territory, hitting an intra-day high of 5095.1 points on the FTSE 100 index by midafternoon, a gain of 1.4 percent on the day.
Buyers were also active on the government bond market, with the key September Gilts contract rising 12/32 to 115-01 just after the Bank of England announcement.
Ciaran Barr, an economist with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said it was important to note that the Bank of England thought rates were now high enough to keep inflation in check.
"That is a clear signal that the Bank thinks it has done enough for the time being and it believes the move should put pressure on sterling," Barr said.
Bank shares also staged a rally on the view that the rate move secured a good environment for further robust earnings growth.
Abbey National rose 12-1/2p to 850p and Lloyds TSB Group 17-1/2p to 784p. Barclays roared to new highs, up 132-1/2p to 1,460p, boosted mainly by results and news of a bigger share buy-back.
In Frankfurt, floor trade ended up two percent at 4414.35, supported by a firm start on Wall Street and receding anxieties about a possible interest rate hike.

The market focus remained on banking shares with Deutsche Bank among the top volume shares, rising 3.05 marks to 119.75 in late trade, amid speculation about further banking industry mergers or takeovers.
The Paris bourse, which ended nearly two percent higher on Wednesday, made further healthy gains on Thursday.
On currency markets, the dollar slipped by half a pfennig in mid-afternoon in sympathy with the sharp selloff in sterling.
"Lower sterling in general is hurting the dollar...and (sterling) was one of the facets of the whole move up," said Richard Vullo, vice president at Bayerische Hypobank in New York.

The U.S. currency was trading at 1.8733 marks, compared to 1.880 beore the Bank of England move. It was also down on the Japanese currency, at 118.35 yen, compared to 118.61 in late Europe on Wednesday.
But sterling was the big loser, slipping five pfennigs to 2.9690 marks from 3.0135 just before the Bank of England announcement. It also fell to $1.5855 from $1.6043 late on Wednesday.
The pound has risen by over 20 percent in the last year, driving down profits at large British exporters.

The Bank of England agreed that the pound was putting "severe pressure" on businesses exposed to international competition, but said its strength mainly reflected factors outside of the Bank's control.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8733 marks and 118.35 yen, compared with 1.8748 and 118.61 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 65.8 points at 5,091.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 78.96 points at 4,414.35 in bourse trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 22.50 points at 3,059.59.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $321.00 an ounce, compared to $319.85 at the close on Wednesday. Silver was one cent up at $4.38.
